verdict.rationale: The firm does publicly disclose concrete pricing for its Clerky-partnered startup formation service ($299 for post-incorporation setup, $149 for managed 83(b) election), which is a genuine instance of public fee transparency. However, this is narrow and limited to one ancillary offering — there is no broader public statement about the firm's rate structures, hourly billing, alternative fee arrangements, or general billing practices across its core practice areas (litigation, M&A, VC, IP, etc.). Missing for 10: firm-wide rate/fee disclosure, AFA policy statements, billing practice transparency beyond the single Clerky product.
